proposals.after: Ding Shoucun, Xu Shou and his son Jian Yin, and Hua Feng.
proposals.reason: Chinese 徐壽子建寅 means Xu Shou and his son Jian Yin; 子 is kinship 'son', not a name element 'Zi'.

proposals.before: Ding Shoucun; Xu Shou; Zi Jianyin; Hua Feng.
proposals.after: Ding Shoucun; Xu Shou; his son Jian Yin; Hua Feng.

proposals.before: His forebears dwelt in Fenghua; from his grandfather's generation they lived in Yin; when Laixian came of age he moved to Tonggu and received inner-school boxing methods from his fellow townsman Shan Sinan.
proposals.after: His forebears dwelt in Fenghua; from his grandfather's generation they lived in Yin; when it came to Laixian he moved to Tonggu and received inner-school boxing methods from his fellow townsman Shan Sinan.
proposals.reason: 至來咸 marks the shift to Laixian's generation, not that he 'came of age'.

proposals.before: Both were guests at a wealthy merchant's house in Yangzhou. Fengchi arrived later and was given the better room above Yulin.
proposals.after: He was a guest at a wealthy merchant's house in Yangzhou. Fengchi arrived later and was lodged above him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 客揚州巨賈家 continues Ma Yulin as subject; it does not say both were guests. The idiomatic 'Both were guests' invents a joint lodging statement not in the source.

proposals.before: Zhou Ji said: "Warfare is peril in the extreme. Unless one has seasoned troops able to engage the enemy in bitter combat for thirty double-hours, and elite vanguard fighters each worth three ordinary men, then even if the commander above is resolute to achieve victory and the ranks below are ready to die for their officers, one cannot be certain of defeating a strong foe.
proposals.after: Zhou Ji said: "Warfare is peril in the extreme. Unless one has seasoned troops able to engage the enemy in bitter combat for thirty ke, and elite vanguard fighters each worth three ordinary men, then even if the commander above is resolute to achieve victory and the ranks below are ready to die for their officers, one cannot be certain of defeating a strong foe.
proposals.reason: 三十刻 uses the clepsydra unit ke, not the double-hour (時辰); rendering 刻 as double-hours inflates the duration and mismatches the idiomatic ke.

proposals.before: Zi was versed in astronomy and mathematics and took part in compiling the Correct Meaning of Pitch Pipes and Calendar. He quarreled with Ferdinand Verbiest and the other Westerners, and they all resented him.
proposals.after: Zi was versed in astronomy and mathematics and took part in compiling the Correct Meaning of the Pitch-pipes. He quarreled with Ferdinand Verbiest and the other Westerners, and they all resented him.
proposals.reason: 律呂正義 is the Kangxi treatise on pitch-pipes/music theory; the idiomatic English wrongly adds “and Calendar,” which is not in the Chinese title.

proposals.before: Zi was versed in astronomy and mathematics and took part in compiling the Correct Meaning of Pitch Pipes and Calendar. He disagreed with Ferdinand Verbiest and the other Westerners, and all bore him ill will.
proposals.after: Zi was versed in astronomy and mathematics and took part in compiling the Correct Meaning of the Pitch-pipes. He disagreed with Ferdinand Verbiest and the other Westerners, and all bore him ill will.
proposals.reason: Same title error as the idiomatic field: 律呂正義 does not include a calendar component in the source wording.

proposals.before: As examiner for the provincial examinations he devised a method of channeling river water into the examination halls through bamboo pipes, which was then regarded as a great convenience.
proposals.after: As supervisor of the provincial examinations he devised a method of channeling river water into the examination halls through bamboo pipes, which was then regarded as a great convenience.
proposals.reason: 鄉試監試 denotes the examination supervisor/proctor, not the chief examiner; 'examiner' overstates the office.

decisions.after: Ding Shoucun, Xu Shou and his son Jianyin, and Hua Feng.
decisions.reason: 徐壽子建寅 means Xu Shou and his son Jianyin; 子 is kinship 'son', not a name element, but the proposed 'Jian Yin' wrongly splits the given name 建寅, which should stay undivided as Jianyin.

decisions.after: Ding Shoucun; Xu Shou; his son Jianyin; Hua Feng.
decisions.reason: Same kinship error in the literal field: 子 means 'son', not Zi; keep 建寅 as the undivided given name Jianyin rather than spaced Jian Yin.
至來咸 marks the generational turn to Laixian, not that he 'came of age'; the proposed literal correctly restores that sense.

After s0063 on Ma Yulin, 客揚州巨賈家 continues him as guest; 鳳池後至，居其上 only adds that Fengchi arrived later and lodged above him, so 'Both were guests' and 'better room' invent unstated joint-lodging detail.
